methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Sampriti Bhattacharyya that has raised $7.2M to date. The transportation sector contains six private peers of varying maturity (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, EarthGrid, and Olympian Motors) and no public comparables. The absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with sufficient data density precludes a reliable peer-median valuation approach.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($7M) as a valuation proxy and applying a standard seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $18M. This reflects typical progression economics for seed-stage companies advancing to Series A, absent material company-specific data skewing this assumption.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M (low) to $21M (high), with a median of $18M. The width of this range reflects limited precision inherent in single-method triangulation. Key uncertainties center on (1) the appropriateness of standard 2.5x step-up multipliers for this particular subsector, (2) the absence of direct peer benchmarking data, and (3) confidence in using total raised as a reliable valuation proxy without additional context on dilution, terms, or market reception. A more robust valuation would benefit from peer-set expansion or disclosure of recent pricing signals.
